items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: At the same festival there were Petula Clark and Charles Aznavour who did not have much fame at that time.

ctx.x: Jean had spoken to the owners of the place where he was working and convinced them that it may be a good idea to have me there for a few days in July and they agreed. The loot wasn't much but they also offered me

room and board for Lily and myself. As a beggar, I couldn't be a chooser. I had a good paying gig in Brittany in a place called Douarnenez the 16th and 17th of July. Lily had taken a train to Royan from Paris and met me when I arrived the afternoon of the 18th. The name of the place where Jean was working was "Cafe de l'Hotel de Ville". It was a brasserie-restaurant and was owned by two very nice people Marcelle and Charles. They had a terrace in front, where we played. We immediately attracted a lot of people…

Lily remained in Royan and I came back after the festival of Complain-la-Tour. People had been missing me and had been screaming my name in the street in front of the Cafe de l'Hotel de Ville. We liked the place, having plenty of good food and drinks. I weighed 150 pounds until I went to this place. When I left there I was hitting the scales at 170 pounds and looking almost as round as Jimmy Rushing. And Lily was almost looking like Ella Fitzgerald.
